rules.text: If the plotted blue markers encode reported case counts by their vertical positions against the y-axis labeled "Count", and the left-to-right x-axis positions represent the displayed reporting progression, then a line whose later-positioned endpoint is higher on the page than its earlier-positioned endpoint indicates a rising reported-case trajectory. If the routing labels are intended to correspond to the named trajectory directions, that trajectory supports the rising-case escalation follow-up route.
rules.conditions: Assumes the y-axis's upward screen direction encodes greater counts, the horizontal order encodes reporting progression, and the route names are semantically matched to the observed trajectory.

rules.text: If the overlapping rotated x-axis inscriptions prevent reliable verification that horizontal position represents chronological reporting order, then the visible upward page geometry alone does not conclusively establish a time-based case trajectory for routing.
rules.conditions: Applies unless the chart's x-axis ordering or time encoding can be verified despite the overlapping labels.

observations.content: The blue line begins with a marker near the bottom-left of the plotting area and ends with a marker near the upper-right.
The vertical axis is visibly labeled "Count" and has printed tick inscriptions including 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, and 1400.
The title visibly reads "Month vs. Number of cases".

refinements.condition_note: These visible tick placements support the condition that higher plotted vertical position corresponds to a greater displayed count; they do not resolve the separate chronological-order condition on the horizontal axis.
refinements.reason: The original chain transcribes the tick values but does not explicitly record their vertical ordering.
